title: Development and Retention of Special Education School Teachers
what_it_is: Development and Retention of Special Education School Teachers

sections.label: SPED schools and SSAs
sections.summary: There are 22 SPED schools led by 12 SSAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we have 22 SPED schools led by 12 SSAs.

sections.label: Additional manpower funding tranches
sections.summary: SPED schools will receive additional funding for manpower costs in two tranches, one implemented in 2021 and another planned for 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To support these efforts, SPED schools will receive additional funding for manpower costs in two tranches: one, which was implemented in 2021, and another planned for 2024.

sections.label: MOE funds SPED teacher training
sections.summary: MOE funds pre-service training for 1,600 SPED teachers through the Diploma in Special Education offered by NIE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Beyond funding and working with SSAs to provide competitive remuneration and meaningful career progression for the 1,600 SPED teachers, MOE funds SPED teachers’ pre-service training in the form of the Diploma in Special Education (DISE) offered by the National Institute of Education (NIE).

sections.label: Questions on SPED teacher targets
sections.summary: A Member asks about meeting projected SPED teacher numbers, pain points preventing recruitment, and the MSF-MOE roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to consider that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, indeed, whenever we review any scheme of service or any benefits, we will certainly take into account all the stakeholders that are involved in taking care of our SPED children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to hear that there are training schemes and even sponsorships for a Masters programme and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But how are we, in terms of meeting the targets that are needed, in terms of the projections of the number of SPED teachers we will need in the coming years and does the Ministry look into what are the current pain points that are preventing people from coming forward, despite all of these very good incentives and training schemes provided?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The other thing is, I am seeing this disconnect, I am a little bit confused – so, I would appreciate the Minister's clarification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that SSAs are coming under MSF, but MOE is now taking a proactive stance in terms of creating the frameworks and training for the SPED teachers.

sections.label: Plan to increase SPED schools
sections.summary: The plan was laid out with MSF, and the number of SPED schools in the system is intended to increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have laid out the plan together with MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We intend to increase the number of SPED schools in our system.

sections.label: Roadmap for SPED teachers, caregivers
sections.summary: A roadmap exists to progressively increase SPED school teachers and caregivers while building infrastructure, reducing reliance on foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we do rely quite a bit on some foreign manpower and, just like any other parts of our education and care sector, we would like a significant core of Singaporeans to be there, so that we can take care of our own people, especially the vulnerable, even amidst possible disruptions in the manpower supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we will want to step up on this and we do have a roadmap worked out on how we progressively increase the number of SPED school teachers and caregivers as we build up the infrastructure in the next few years.

sections.label: SPED school to post-18 continuum
sections.summary: The next lap's biggest gap is providing a continuum from the school system to post-18 arrangements to support the SPED community and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In our next lap, the biggest gap will be how we provide a continuum from the school system to the post-18 arrangement so that we can better support the SPED community, including the caregivers, who will always be worried about what will happen to their special needs children when they are no longer around.

sections.label: SPED community beyond educators
sections.summary: Beyond SPED educators, allied educators and physiotherapists form the wider community, and the Member's requested number can be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As what Ms Denise Phua has said, beyond the SPED educators, we have another group of people, which includes the allied educators, physiotherapists and so forth who form the entire community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I can get the Member the number that he had asked for.
